questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really have a specific idea about what I wanted from my exchange, but I choose Oulu because i wanted to go to the north

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic was not good, but the place was beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: easy enough to find the guide for the orientation, but not easy to figure out the courses

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a Finnish girl who helped us with information about the place

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy, because they have a housing company for students, which most people use. It's called psoas.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: All students live off campus, and if you rent through psoas you live with all the other exchange students. It can become a bit much with the noise.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There where no things in the apartment, you have to buy everything yourself.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They don't have a OLA so i had to fill it out the old school way which took me a time to figure out because there are two schools with the name university of oulu, but the one called Applied science has a OLA, and you might apply for the wrong university.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to show your english level, fill out a LA and choose courses from the university.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could write the study counselor for the science department

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It was difficult, given that the school doesn't have many, so you are very limited in the choosing.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They have a lot of weird courses, and it is very old school, so i found that the book exams made a lot of sense for me, so you can work in your own pace, they do not have a lot of classes a week, so you have a lot of free time. Therefore a book exam is a great opportunity

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The academic level is not very high. It was not difficult. But it was very difficult to understand the teachers, they don't speak English very well

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Not high

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very chill. In some courses I barely had any classes. They separated us from the Finnish students so we had very few classes in compared to the finnish.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.answer:

questions.answer: The supermarkets are very expensive in Finland, and alcohol

questions.answer: Nothing, the rest is danish prices

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of different stuff. I did not engage so much myself

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Non, maybe sauna

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Watch the auroras, take a trip to Helsinki, take a trip to Lapland

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It wasn't a culture shock, but it was a bit different. Its more chill than Copenhagen, you have more freetime.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are very open in general, so its easy if you want

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: They have a more equal view on the sexes

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The equality between man and woman

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: They need to be prepared for a lot of freetime, its not cheap in finland and the academic level is not high.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, maybe find housing though something else than psoas, if you want a nice place, it is very basic and not very nice

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: To see the Nature in Finland, it is very beautiful

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The courses, getting it to fit with my 30 credits. It was almost impossible, and the school did not help much.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
